Alphabet (GOOGL): key metrics through the third quarter of 2026

GOOGL-zbar-2026-10-28 · USD · series 2026-10-29T18:41:24Z · built 2026-10-29 18:41 UTC

As of 2026-10-29 (ET). Status: pending more analysis. Third-quarter figures come from the earnings release (Oct 28) and the quarterly report (10-Q, filed Oct 29); each figure cites the filing that printed it first.

Alphabet took in $127.6 billion in the quarter, up 24.6% from a year ago, and operating income rose 29.9% to $40.6 billion. Cloud revenue doubled (+103%) to $30.7 billion and its operating profit rose from $3.6 billion to $11.1 billion. Search grew 12% to $63.4 billion, its slowest pace this year, on 8% more paid clicks at 4% higher prices per click. Earnings per share still fell, from $2.87 to $2.12: other income swung from +$12.8 billion to −$8.2 billion as the value of Alphabet's stock holdings fell, which by Alphabet's count took $0.55 a share off the quarter.

Capital spending was $51.4 billion, more than the $42.3 billion of operating cash, so free cash flow was −$9.1 billion, the second negative quarter running. Long-term debt reached $125.1 billion, up from $46.5 billion at year-end. Alphabet bought back no stock, against $11.5 billion a year ago.¹ Instead it sold new shares: in Q3 Alphabet sold 36 million new shares through its at-the-market program (12 million Class A for $4.3 billion, 24 million Class C for $8.1 billion, $27.6 billion of the program left), on top of 86 million sold in June in a public offering and a placement with Berkshire Hathaway. Common shares outstanding rose 64 million in Q3, to 12.29 billion, including employee stock.

It also issued mandatory convertible preferred stock in June: 385 million depositary shares, each a twentieth of a preferred share, so about 19.25 million preferred shares (the balance sheet rounds to 19 million; $18.0 billion carrying value; 6.25% dividend). Each preferred share turns into common stock on or about May 15, 2029: 2.2520 to 2.8160 Class A shares for Series A and 2.2740 to 2.8420 Class C shares for Series B, fewer shares the higher the stock price. That adds roughly 44 to 54 million shares, which would take the 12.29 billion common shares to about 12.34 to 12.35 billion (calculated). Capped calls Alphabet bought would offset part of that if the stock rises, and they aren't counted here.

Close competitors

  • Microsoft: Azure competes with Google Cloud for AI and enterprise workloads; Bing and Copilot compete for search questions.
  • Amazon: AWS is the largest cloud rival, and Amazon's store ads compete for product-search ad budgets.
  • Meta: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp compete for the same brand and performance ad budgets.
  • OpenAI: ChatGPT competes for questions that used to start as a Google search.

No peer figures are shown. Microsoft and Meta figures are not in this page yet. Amazon's AWS and Google Cloud are reported on different bases, so a side-by-side number would mislead. OpenAI is private and files no public reports.

For the week of Oct 19: $53,273M ÷ 12,309M shares = $4.33 of free cash flow a share, and $332.08 ÷ $4.33 = 76.7×; the weeks of Oct 5, Oct 12 and Oct 19 read 80.6×, 80.6× and 76.7×. The line is drawn for the weeks of Sep 28, 2020 to Jun 21, 2021 (29.6× to 32.9×) and from the week of Sep 27, 2021 on.
  • Why $53.3 billion and not $19.7 billion. Both are Alphabet's printed trailing free cash flow. $53.3 billion covers the four quarters through June: Q3'25 $24.5B + Q4'25 $24.6B + Q1'26 $10.1B + Q2'26 −$5.9B. The Q3 release's $19.7 billion covers the four quarters through September: Q3'25's $24.5 billion drops out and Q3'26's −$9.1 billion comes in. The weekly line moves to $19.7 billion together with the P/E's earnings; Q3 results are not yet in the trailing figure.

Risks

  • Search slows. Search growth went from 19% to 17% to 12% this year, and the quarter's Search dollars were flat against the second quarter, so Cloud now supplies most of the growth.
  • Spending overtook cash in the last two quarters. Free cash flow was −$5.9 billion in Q2 and −$9.1 billion in Q3. Over the last twelve months, capital spending of $159.8 billion against $179.6 billion of operating cash leaves $19.7 billion of free cash flow, down from $73.6 billion a year earlier.
  • Dilution replaces buybacks. No stock was bought back for three quarters. In Q3 Alphabet sold 36 million new shares through its at-the-market program; common shares outstanding rose 64 million, to 12.29 billion, including employee stock. The convertible preferred adds roughly 44 to 54 million more in May 2029.
  • Reported earnings swing with the portfolio. Gains on stock holdings inflate trailing earnings (other income was $98.0 billion in the second quarter alone), so trailing earnings overstate what the operating business alone earns.

Against its own history

  • Cloud operating margin: 36.2%, against 23.7% a year ago (calculated).
  • YouTube ads: +9.2% to $11.2 billion, slower than the second quarter's 13%.
  • Traffic acquisition costs: 20.0% of ad revenue, about level with a year ago (calculated).
  • Revenue per employee (trailing twelve months): $2.30 million, against $2.03 million a year ago. Headcount was 204,757, up 7.7% (calculated).
  • Net income per employee: $1.15 million. Securities gains inflate it, so read revenue per employee for the business.
